title: Exploratory contextual severity triage pilot
status: Revision-stage exploratory policy replay; not part of the original thirteen targets. Original detector outcomes were already known. This plan is frozen before computing the new pilot summaries; this is not independent preregistration.
research_question: How do explicit operational context and retained class uncertainty change severity-aware human triage, and what is the incremental Pi CPU cost?
sampling: Use every saved record in each population without exclusions. Report populations separately; they overlap and are not independent replications. Reusing a flow across hypothetical profiles does not create new independent observations.

profiles.description: Hypothetical noncritical asset with no reported operational impact; attack evidence gives Low triage severity.
Hypothetical production-critical asset with no reported operational impact; attack evidence gives Moderate triage severity.
Hypothetical independently reported serious operational impact; High triage severity overrides a Normal model label. This supplied scenario is not an observed dataset impact.
No usable asset/impact context; severity remains unassigned and context review is required.

severity_levels.Not_indicated: No attack indicated by the evaluated candidate labels; this does not certify absence of harm.
severity_levels.Low: Human review for possible attack on the noncritical hypothetical asset.
severity_levels.Moderate: Prioritized human review for possible attack on the critical hypothetical asset.
severity_levels.High: Urgent human review because serious impact was supplied independently of the model.
severity_levels.Unassigned: Context or model information is insufficient; request review.

rules: Known serious-impact report overrides all model outputs and assigns High plus review.
Unknown context returns Unassigned plus context review.
Any non-Normal candidate assigns Low in P1 or Moderate in P2, with review.
For confidence-aware modes, the inherited written-confidence floor 0.50 triggers review; it never scales the positive severity tier.

For the uncertainty mode, candidates are the union of the greedy label and the original nominal-95% prediction set. Empty/invalid sets require model review. Existing alert evidence is never discarded.
If only Normal is indicated with no review trigger, return Not_indicated/routine. Model review without attack evidence returns Unassigned.
No mitigation, blocking, isolation or external notification is executed.

modes.label_only: Greedy-label diagnostic baseline, without the floor.
modes.confidence_floor: Greedy label plus the inherited 0.50 confidence floor; main baseline.
modes.set_augmented: Greedy label union retained prediction set, plus the same floor; main comparison.

primary_metrics: True attacks assigned routine: count and rate among true attacks
True Normal records sent to review: count and rate among true Normal
Additional attack referrals and additional Normal referrals relative to confidence-floor baseline
metric_interpretation: Attack/Normal truth assesses missed referrals and review burden only. No observed severity, impact, safety or operational-outcome labels exist. Do not report severity accuracy, severity F1, harm reduction or calibrated risk. Low/Moderate/High are authored demonstration policy choices, not mappings prescribed or endorsed by NIST/CISA.
uncertainty_reporting: Descriptive exact counts and denominators. No p-values or confidence intervals that treat repeated scenario cases or duplicate input blocks as independent incidents.
implementation_checks: Prediction-set expansion cannot suppress an existing referral
Known criticality cannot reduce the positive severity tier
For fixed non-Normal evidence, confidence never changes Low/Moderate/High
timing: Local and Pi resident-memory replay using identical JSON inputs and Python standard library. Five warmup batches then thirty timed batches over both primary modes and all four profiles. Report median/p95 batch time normalized by decisions and full-batch time; parsing/setup are separate. No model calls and no claim of end-to-end detection or attribution latency.
evidence: Preserve policy, data/code hashes, per-record output ledger, exact aggregates, device metadata and independent arithmetic checks. Sources unchanged.

references.title: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security
references.use: Contextual rationale: OT risk assessment considers operational and safety consequences and organizational impact categories; it does not supply or validate this pilot policy.

references.title: CISA National Cyber Incident Scoring System
references.use: Contextual rationale: severity/priority depends on impact and recovery context; the present pilot does not implement NCISS.
